summary: Edge fanout routing mismatch causing priority starvation and elevated 5xx rate for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 02:14 UTC Lexa Health reported a sudden spike in 502/503 and aborted streaming sessions from their inference endpoints. Impact: ~35-45% of requests returned 5xx over a ~45 minute window; customer-facing app reported large retry storms and timeouts. Environment: prod-us-east, customer on Dedicated pool 'lexa-dedicated-pool-3' with autoscaling disabled.

Observed behavior: Short text-generation calls (<=64 tokens) frequently received upstream 502 with body 'upstream unavailable' and streaming sessions dropped mid-response with TLS reset. Runtime logs show repeated worker exits (exit code 137) and watchdog restarts around the same timestamps. Edge proxy metrics show an unusual imbalance in route weight assignments: the prefetch route for lexaprefetch/* was fanouting significantly more connections than expected and consuming a high percentage of keepalive slots on the edge proxy.

Steps to reproduce:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.prod.lexa/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"gptx-6b-q4","input":"short prompt"}' --repeat during a busy tenant period
2) Observe intermittent 502/503 and streaming disconnects after ~200-400ms.

Initial hypothesis: Edge route assignment mismatch allowed prefetch-style requests to be elevated to a higher fanout path without respecting per-tenant concurrency bounds. This created connection pool starvation at the edge proxy which cascaded back to the serving-runtime, causing queue growth and out-of-memory worker restarts under load.

Evidence collected:
- Edge proxy keepalive occupancy spike (keepalive_in_use 93% -> 99% for 02:10-02:55 UTC).
- Per-route connection histogram showing lexaprefetch/* opened 4-6x expected concurrent sockets.
- Runtime logs: repeated "worker killed by OOM" and NVML logs showing GPU memory fragmentation and allocations failing around same timestamps.
- API gateway traces show heavy retry storms from SDK clients.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Applied temporary rate limit on lexaprefetch/* at the edge (reduced burst size from 300 -> 40).
- Scaled dedicated pool 'lexa-dedicated-pool-3' +1 node to absorb backlog.
- Rolled a hotfix to edge proxy config to enforce per-tenant keepalive caps.

Result: Error rate returned to baseline (~<1.5% 5xx) within 20 minutes of mitigations. Customer reported resumed normal operation and accepted temporary limit while we implemented a permanent fix.

investigation_notes: Correlation between edge-proxy keepalive slots and runtime OOMs indicates the issue originated at route assignment layer. Edge config allowed lexaprefetch to be assigned to an experimental high-fanout weight during recent routing reshuffle. That experimental path did not enforce per-tenant caps. Investigation traced change to routing rollout PR #4679 (route-weight-sweep) which mis-tagged lexaprefetch.
root_cause_summary: A recent routing weight reshuffle accidentally escalated a prefetch route into a high-fanout path without enforcing per-tenant concurrency and keepalive caps. This caused the edge proxy to exhaust keepalive slots, leading to connection queueing backpressure on serving runtime and worker OOMs, producing elevated 5xx responses.
resolution: Merged PR #4821 to add enforcement of per-tenant keepalive/concurrency ceilings and fixed route tagging logic. Deployed hotfix to prod-us-east 2026-03-13 04:10 UTC. Added an alert that triggers at 75% keepalive utilization per-proxy and a prefetch circuit-breaker that soft-limits fanout for any single tenant.
postmortem_followups: Schedule rollback-safe canary for routing-weight sweeps and require per-route cap unit tests (owner: Platform Eng, target: 2026-03-20)
Add SLO-based runbook step to auto-apply per-tenant soft-rate-limit when keepalive utilization > 80% (owner: SRE, target: 2026-03-17)
Re-run tenant-level chaos tests that simulate heavy prefetch fanout (owner: QA, target: 2026-03-18)
